done.why: I had seen a good stretch of the early caverns. My contrary pokes at the menhir only got flat refusals, so I left before finding the pearls or the stone door.

about: A Zork-style underground cavern adventure. A Wizard has hoarded the Empire's treasures south of a ravine. You explore a barrow, a cavern, a formal garden and a carousel room.

moments.note: Eating the lantern got a joking refusal that called it a lamp.
The Wizard appeared and his look told me where the treasure lay, then he fumbled my lamp.
The compound command to take the sword and polish it failed with 'can't see any such thing'.
Going northeast from the Great Cavern put me on the Foot Bridge.
The newspaper had a funny, hint-laden story about the Wizard.
The carousel room explained that the floor was turning under me.

wished: Push the menhir with the sword or find the carousel's works.
Find the stone door and the pearls.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you
lines.why: It pointed me at the goal in character.

lines.line: The floor, you realize a moment too late, has been turning under you the whole time
lines.why: It gave a small, vivid reveal.

fun.why: The jokes and the Wizard encounter were fun, but parser refusals slowed it down.

engagement.why: I had a clear goal, but I left before getting far.

difficulty.why: It was fair, but the menhir and the carousel blocked me.

interestingness.why: It is a familiar Zork world with fresh touches in the Wizard's behaviour.

prose.why: The prose was witty and clean.
